subject.title: Feature request: first-class async result routing back to originating topic sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class core async route registry for external-event-to-topic-session callbacks, or keep the registry outside core behind plugin/API seams?
rationale: The request crosses event source ownership, persistent route state, matching confidence, dedupe, privacy redaction, approval policy, visible channel delivery, and targeted session wake behavior, so current source cannot choose the product boundary safely.

options.title: Prefer plugin/API seams
options.body: Keep core lean and identify only the missing generic APIs needed for a ClawHub/plugin implementation of async route registries.

options.title: Sponsor core v1
options.body: Define a small Gateway-owned registry with explicit SQLite storage, matcher, privacy, dedupe, and safe-action contracts.

options.title: Defer broad layer
options.body: Continue landing only narrow hook, wake, and async-continuation fixes until demand or a missing API seam is clearer.

recommendation.title: Prefer plugin/API seams
recommendation.body: Keep core lean and identify only the missing generic APIs needed for a ClawHub/plugin implementation of async route registries.

likelyOwner.reason: The history points to steipete across the current routing snapshot, hook mapping feature, and adjacent wake-targeting code, making them the best available product-boundary owner from this evidence.
